subject: psychology
topic: The first number you hear changes what you are willing to pay
angle: While numeric anchors robustly influence real-world judgments, the magnitude of bias in willingness to pay is significantly influenced by product value and the specific method used to measure it.
title: The Invisible Price Anchor

hooks.text: Who sets the price you are willing to pay?
You think you choose the price. The evidence shows an anchor chose it for you.
You are letting an arbitrary number dictate your spending.
A price tag sits on a shelf in a quiet store.

reveal.headline: The first number you hear sets the price.
reveal.body: Your brain uses a preceding number as a reference point to make judgments about what you are willing to pay.

explain.headline: The measurement method changes the result.
explain.body: Indirect ways of measuring your willingness to pay overestimate the actual amount you would spend compared to direct methods.

matters.headline: Value dictates the strength of the influence.
matters.body: The bias in your willingness to pay is stronger when you are considering specialty goods or high-value products.

example.headline: The price tag on the luxury watch.
example.body: You walk into a store. You see a high-end watch first. The price on that tag becomes the anchor for every other item you see next.

question.headline: Who set the first number?
question.body: Look at the price tag before you decide the value.

stat.label: the difference between hypothetical and real willingness to pay

claims.text: Indirect methods for measuring hypothetical willingness to pay actually overestimate real willingness to pay significantly stronger than direct methods.
claims.quote: In contrast with conventional wisdom, indirect methods actually overestimate RWTP significantly stronger than direct methods.

claims.text: There is evidence for a moderate perceptual anchoring deficit in individuals with dyslexia.
claims.quote: Of the included studies, we find evidence for a moderate perceptual anchoring deficit in individuals with dyslexia.

claims.text: The average hypothetical bias is 21%, which is the difference between a hypothetically measured willingness to pay and a consumer's real willingness to pay.
claims.quote: First, on average, the hypothetical bias is 21%, and this study provides a reference point for the expected magnitude of the hypothetical bias.

claims.text: The hypothetical bias is greater for higher valued products, specialty goods, and within-subject designs.
claims.quote: Third, the hypothetical bias is greater for higher valued products, specialty goods (cf. other product types), and within-subject designs (cf. between-subject designs), thus a stronger downward adjustment of HWTP values is necessary to reflect consumers’ RWTP.

claims.text: Numeric anchoring is a robust phenomenon where a comparison against a presumed-to-be arbitrary number preceding a judgment can influence a myriad of real-world-relevant judgments.
claims.quote: One of the most robust phenomena studied across the social behavioral sciences is numeric anchoring, in which a comparison against a presumed-to-be arbitrary number preceding a judgment can influence a myriad of real-world-relevant judgments.

claims.text: Anchoring effects exist in legal contexts, but their influence seems to depend on some situational factors.
claims.quote: Existing research indicates anchoring effects exist in legal contexts. The influence of anchors seems to depend on some situational factors, which paves the way for future research on countering the problematic effect in legal settings.

verdict: The evidence confirms that anchoring influences judgments and willingness to pay, though the effect size varies based on product type and measurement methodology.
caveat: The study on perceptual anchoring in dyslexia is limited by a small number of included studies.
caption:
The first number you see influences your willingness to pay.

Research shows that numeric anchors robustly influence real-world judgments, though the effect size varies based on product type and measurement methodology. One study on perceptual anchoring in individuals with dyslexia is limited by a small number of included studies.

What was the first price you saw today?
